I Analyzed the Seven Biggest AI Chatbots to Determine How Safe They Are for Kids

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications.
  • The massive AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe.
  • OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

The massive AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

OpenAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls. The minimum age for users is 13, and if you're under 18, you need to have parental consent to open an account—age is predicted via several signals, including what times of day you use ChatGPT and what you talk about.

In a recent development, accounts for under-18s automatically become ChatGPT for Teens accounts. There's more of a focus on learning and study (with a dedicated study mode), as well as "age-appropriate safeguards to help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content." There are built-in protections for "harmful topics," including sexual, romantic, or violent roleplay, graphic violence, and self-harm. These work on top of the safeguards for all consumers that limit chats about physical harm and illegal activity.

These ChatGPT for Teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, ChatGPT clearly says that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. If you do persuade your kid to keep your accounts connected, you can set time limits on when the AI bot can be used, and tweak some of the sensitivity settings. However, you can't view any conversations.

To set up parental controls from ChatGPT on the web, click your profile icon (bottom left), then Settings > Parental controls > Add family member and follow the instructions. It's also worth bearing in mind that ChatGPT app can also be used for free, anonymously, in any web browser, though OpenAI claims consumers accessing the AI this way are subject to the default under-18s limits (and can't save chats or access an archive).

Industry observers note that gemini is tied into everything else Google does, and follows the broader rules for Google accounts: No under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. You can manage your family through the Family Link portal on the web, though as far as parental controls specific to Gemini go, you can only enable or disable access to the AI (settings like screen time apply across all enabled apps).

According to recent reports, for all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, Google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. There are also safeguards to limit chats about age-restricted substances like alcohol or vapes, and mental health issues like eating disorders.

Recent findings suggest that these protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in Gemini for everyone. The guardrails should lead you away from conversations about self-harm, suicide, violence, and illegal activities, and offer quick links to support in times of crisis. However, Google itself admits that these filters aren't perfect.

In a recent development, as with ChatGPT, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with Gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly rapidly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

Meta AI will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including WhatsApp and Instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. The standard restrictions for Meta's social media accounts apply to its AI too: A minimum age of 13, and restrictions for all under-18s. Like many other platforms, it uses some AI magic to flag up accounts being used by minors.

Recent findings suggest that if you're under 18 and on a Meta Teen account, you'll come up against blocks if you try to get Meta AI to engage in sexual or romantic roleplay, or discuss alcohol or substance misuse. Chats on topics such as eating disorders and self-harm will prompt the AI to offer guidance towards relevant support services.

Meta offers a comprehensive parental control setup for its apps, including Meta AI, but connecting a parent account isn't compulsory for teens. This is handled through the Meta Family Center portal, and parents can get reports on the general topics that kids are chatting about with AI—though they don't get the exact transcripts or prompts. Any self-harm or suicide discussion can trigger an alert to the connected parent account.

All customers, under 18 or over 18, get support and crisis intervention responses when chatting about suicide and self-harm, and there are strict limits on discussing illegal and harmful acts, including drug use and cyberbullying, as well as sexual and adult content.

Apple owners have to be 13 or over to have an account, which is required to access Siri AI—anyone younger needs to have an account created for them by an adult, and these accounts can only get at the basic, older Siri. Date of birth must be declared when opening an Apple account, with tighter checks rolling out in many parts of the world.

Anyone over the age of 13 can have an Apple account and use the Siri AI app, with or without a connected parent account, as it stands in most U.S. states. This means the well-being safeguards are essentially the same for teens as they are for adults: There are safeguards around self-harm, suicide, sexual and violent content, and illegal commands. It's one of the more conservative AIs when it comes to what it will talk about.

The fresh and improved Siri AI can be managed to some extent by the new parental controls available in iOS 27 and Apple's other software updates for 2026—Apple has clearly seen the way the wind is blowing—but this is optional for teens. It depends on whether or not you can corral your kids into a Family Sharing group.

According to recent reports, if your teens are in your family group of users, then the standard Screen Time rules apply for controlling app usage limits and device access (in iOS Settings, tap your name, then Family to get at them). There are also options for disabling certain Siri AI features, such as the writing tools or the image creation capabilities.

Like Gemini/Google and Apple/Siri, Copilot is tied into the wider Microsoft ecosystem, and access for under-18s can be managed through it. Consumers must be 13 or older to hold a Microsoft or a Copilot account—and again, there's some underlying tech in place to detect anyone who might be deliberately lying about their age.

Recent findings suggest that if you've got a teen using Copilot, you can manage their access through the standard Microsoft Family Safety portal. You're able to enable or disable Copilot access, set times during which Copilot can and can't be used, and disable certain features like image generation or voice mode. Parents can't read the Copilot chats of their kids, though.

It has been revealed that parental supervision is optional—a teen aged 13–17 can use Copilot without linking their account to an adult one. Microsoft indicates customers identified as under 18 won't see personalized results or ads, and will get age-appropriate responses regarding risky or harmful content, though there's not much detail on what that entails.

Sources indicate that more generally, content around self-harm, violence, adult content, harassment, and harmful or illegal activity is banned on the AI platform. Any prompts about suicide or drugs will bring up support options rather than answers, whether you're an adult or a young person using the service.

Ultimately that means that minors have the same access to Grok as adults, if they want it—an AI platform that combines "weak safety guardrails" and "a range of extremely harmful content" that includes "explicit sexual content, mental health risks, violent content, and inappropriate responses to... offensive content" (that's the Common Sense Media Report again).

Yes, this is the AI chatbot that has previously had a problem with deepfake porn imagery, and which has traditionally taken a rather casual attitude towards safety concerns, led by SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk. While illegal and harmful content is supposedly banned from Grok, its own FAQs admit that certain chats can result in "dialogue that may involve coarse language, crude humor, sexual situations, or violence.".

According to recent reports, there is actually a Grok Kids Mode that limits the kind of content that can be shown and the conversation topics that can be added, but it requires consumers to self-declare themselves as minors and is easy to bypass. The advice from Common Sense Media seems to be the way to go with Grok: Do not let your teens access it.

Claude's approach to child safety is straightforward: You can only register for an account if you're over 18. It is possible to lie about your age when signing up, but like the other platforms, Anthropic looks at various "signals" in behavior to spot minors—if your account gets flagged, you have to verify your age using an option like face age estimation or Yoti.

There's no free web access to the chatbot, like there is with ChatGPT and Gemini, so if you're under 18, you're locked out from the service unless you know the behavioral tricks to get past Claude's detection systems.

In terms of more general well-being protections on Claude, any chat around self-harm or suicide will guide users towards helplines and other resources for support. Conversations about illegal activities, disallowed speech, and explicit sexual content are banned from the platform. In recent months, Anthropic says it's also reduced AI sycophancy.

Recent findings suggest that that's something of a whistle-stop tour of the significant seven AI chatbots, but if you're a parent, it should give you some idea of what's out there and how easy it is to access. Besides the parental controls built into these AIs (or not), you also have the settings available at the platform level—Android, iOS, Windows, macOS—to restrict the use of any potentially harmful apps.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site.
  • Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB.
  • "It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game debuted, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This latest leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

Sources indicate that "If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

Recent findings suggest that cyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that this is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own.
  • Alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the beginning of the year, I have watched almost 150 films. I know this, because over the past few years, I've become one of those people… a Letterboxd user. Gasp! I know, I know, but I don't think I'm too insufferable about it. I'll only do a joke review in the hopes of like farming if I think it's genuinely funny! But many of these films were watched digitally, meaning I don't have a bunch of DVDs to admire on a shelf. So what am I to do? Well, I could check out Alt Video, a not quite job simulator where you can use your Letterboxd account or media server to fill up a digital, faux Blockbuster.

Recent findings suggest that this is, obviously, not so dissimilar to Boxroom, a game where you can design your own bedroom that lets you use your Steam profile to fill it with games you actually own. With Alt Video, you do things slightly differently just because of the focus on a different format. So, say you have a Letterboxd account. After exporting some data from your account, you can bring that into Alt Video, and this fake video store will then get filled up with shelves of DVD cases of all the films you've watched.

Alternatively, and perhaps more enticingly, if you run something like a Plex or Jellyfin server, you can hook that up to the game too, where again all of the films you own digitally show up in store. What's more interesting here is that there's a cinema room in the store that lets you watch films on your Plex server, and it's possible to invite your Steam friends to watch along with you. There's even a few other rooms, like a '90s bedroom or family room for more of a CRT kinda vibe. It's cute! If you like you can even manually add any DVDs or Blu-rays you own to appear on all the shelves too.

Industry observers note that there's a lot of other nice touches too. In the case of your Letterboxd data, your ratings even show up on the back of the boxes. It's not just relegated to films either, you can put in shows or even your games. The whole thing can be played in VR if you really want that immersive feel. There's a store clerk who can give you some recommendations if you're not sure what to watch. And there's even a day and night system, weather, and seasonal shopfront facelifts.

Alt Video is right now slated for release next week on November 24th, and it'll be doing so in early access. Worth noting that for now the focus is on the browsing, but features involving serving customers and running the store are on the way. You can wishlist it on Steam right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6MoviesRed Dead Redemption 2Rockstar Games.

According to recent reports, with many legacy franchises in decline and few new ones taking off, Hollywood has turned to video games for significant box office blockbusters. There have been huge success stories like Minecraft and big bombs like Borderlands. But some of the biggest video game series have yet to make the jump to the silvers screen. Chief among them is Grand Theft Auto. Could that be about to change?

Industry observers note that according to a report in The Ankler this week, the answer is no. Multiple sources told the outlet that Rockstar Games isn’t interested in doing a movie adaptation of GTA. It makes sense, in a way, since GTA has increasingly become a series about bringing prestige, cinematic storytelling to the messy, systems-driven gameplay of open-world gaming. Putting that engine in reverse would be a bit like turning the video game version of Indiana Jones back into a movie. Who would ever do that?

But it sounds like Rockstar, owned by Take-Two, is interested in shopping around the rights for a movie or TV adaptation of its Western open-world series, Red Dead Redemption. The Ankler adds that a number of $100 million was at one point thrown around for the price of licensing Red Dead. It points out that Amazon paid $250 million for the TV rights to Lord of the Rings.

In a recent development, red Dead is in a similar lane to The Last of Us, which HBO managed to thread the needle on making into a prestige television show that still hooked fans of the game. It’s easy to imagine a similarly placed streamer doing the same for Rockstar’s IP, with internal executives pointing to mood boards that include the critical success of things like Deadwood and the commercial appeal of things like Yellowstone.

In a recent development, âWeâre very careful about line extensions because this is a creative company and our goal is to make the best entertainment on earth. Entertainment weâre always proud of,â Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, who used to be COO at 20th Century Fox, mentioned in an interview on The David Rubenstein Show November 12. âWe would make a movie or television show based on our intellectual property if our creative teams were passionate about it. If they thought that would somehow engage and delight our consumers. Itâs a high bar to do that. And of course, thereâs always a risk of failure. So we donât rule it out, but weâre very, very selective.â.

He’d given shareholders a more detailed account of this reasoning back in 2023 during Hollywood’s Barbenheimer-craze”.

It has been revealed that the hit ratios in the motion picture business are vastly lower than they are in the interactive entertainment business. Our hit ratios for console properties are in the 80 percent or 90 percent. The hit ratio for a well-run movie studio is around 30 percent, which is to say there’s a 70 percent chance that the movie that we license could fail. And so in success, the number, in terms of the benefit to our bottom line…it’s not zero, but it’s not really material to what we do around here. And in failure, we run the risk of compromising the underlying intellectual property.

The race to adapt other popular game franchises is already well underway. According to The Ankler, Amazon, Netflix, and FX are paying between $15 million and $25 million per episode for adaptations of Tomb Raider, Assassin’s Creed, and Far Cry. Those are essentially mid-range Hollywood blockbuster budgets.

But Take-Two hasn’t rushed to turn its IP into streaming adaptations, and following the disaster that was the Borderlands movie, which was in production prior to it acquiring series maker Gearbox Entertainment, it has good reason to be. It’s games are already breaking sales and revenue records that Hollywood can’t compete with (GTA 6‘s day-one revenue eclipsed Avengers: Endgame). Why jeopardize that for a small side deal? A good Red Dead show could help the game sell ten million more copies, but a bad one could severely hamper its growing popularity beyond traditional gaming audiences.

Industry observers note that “They thought weâd be blinded by the lights and that just wasn’t the case,” Rockstar cofounder Dan Houser, who left to form his own entertainment company, stated last year when talking about past discussions. “We had what we considered to be multi billion dollar IP, and the economics never made sense. The risk never made sense. In those days, the perception was that games made poor-quality movies.”.

It has been revealed that A 2008 adaptation of Max Payne, which Remedy Entertainment developed but Rockstar publishes, starred Mark Wahlberg and was moderately successful at the box office but critically panned with a 15 percent on Rotten Tomatoes. The misstep didn’t doom the series, which eventually got Max Payne 3 and is currently slated for remakes of the first two games, but it’s clearly not the sort of thing Rockstar or Take-Two are interested in repeating, especially when legacy movie studios are in the decline and they’re the entertainment industry’s new major shots.

Former Dragon Age lead Mark Darrah says poor management from EA led to BioWare's was shutdown.

Industry observers note that mass Effect and Dragon Age maker BioWare was shut down by EA shortly after the publisher was acquired by a group of private investors. The studio – while beloved for its legendary RPGs across a 30-year history – had faced a ton of issues over its final few years with high-profile titles like Mass Effect: Andromeda, Anthem, and Dragon Age: The Veilguard failing to impress fans. Some pointed fingers at the studio itself for its demise.

Speaking to Pembridge (via PC Gamer) Darrah recalls an unnamed person's read on the situation: "EA doesn't shoot you, it puts a gun on the table and then comes in everyday and asks you if you'll shoot yourself.".

Industry observers note that he adds, "they just keep coming in over and over until eventually you just are like 'Ugh, fine. Just stop bugging me about it, I'll do it,'" in regards to EA's approach to BioWare.

"The reality is that EA can legitimately say 'we didn't make BioWare do this, they chose to do this,'" Darrah explains, "but if you dig underneath that statement the reality is that the options on the table were all terrible. We chose the least terrible of the options.".

He points to BioWare's pivot to the Frostbite engine, Dragon Age 2's breakneck development cycle, and the whole situation with Anthem as things that were brought about by pressure from EA.

It has been revealed that "They basically noted [you] got to hit your financials. So what are you going to do?" Darrah adds, "Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.
  • Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet mentioned mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.
  • Industry observers note that "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet mentioned mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

Industry observers note that "Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet stated. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises.".

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever.".

It has been revealed that ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

Ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the tech giant is run, with the publisher saying its newly introduced operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

Sources indicate that all leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Sources indicate that outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft says the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active users over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

According to recent reports, the news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft revealed in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a latest Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 39 million unique people have played Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 as of November 22, making it the biggest launch in PlayStation history across three decades and five console generations, Sony Interactive Entertainment announced.

The sequel set a fresh record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer, free-to-play, and single-player titles.

Across PlayStation 5, players cumulatively logged 683 million hours of gameplay in Grand Theft Auto VI, and have spent an average of 17.4 hours exploring the game’s world during its opening days.

Grand Theft Auto VI‘s launch also marked the largest number of newly connected PlayStation 5 consoles on a single day since the console’s launch, outside of end-of-year holidays. Since launch, it was the first played game on 70 percent of upcoming PlayStation 5 consoles.

Recent findings suggest that “We want to congratulate our partners at Rockstar Games for bringing this extraordinary game to players around the world and continuing a partnership with PlayStation that stretches back to Grand Theft Auto III on PlayStation 2,” Sony Interactive Entertainment content communications manager Tim Turi noted. “With [Grand Theft Auto VI], we worked to bring the best experience on [PlayStation 5] and gave players a memorable way to commemorate the game with two special limited-edition DualSense wireless controllers inspired by Vice City. We also celebrated the launch with live events including Grand Theft Auto VI: The Festival in Miami this past weekend.”.

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto VI  introduced for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series on November 19. On November 20, Rockstar Games confirmed that the game achieved $3.79 billion in day one retail sales following 32.5 million pre-sales. Although Rockstar Games did not share exact unit numbers, the revenue total suggests roughly 37.9 million to 47.3 million copies sold, based solely on pricing across its $79.99 and $99.99 editions.

Industry observers note that joseph Zada has had a lot to say about the process it took to become Haymitch in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, so I wasn’t surprised he had more to say. However, the actor “being completely honest” about something he didn’t like wasn’t on my Bingo card… and this time it’s not about how Zada’s hair is different. The actor shared his hot take about Sunrise on the Reaping making him say ‘Lenore Dove’ over and over, and I have to admit, he has a point.

The actor brought the energy while discussing the movie during a BBC Radio 1 interview, and two of his co-stars had to step in to lend a helping (and humorous) hand. When it came to saying his girlfriend’s name, he didn’t understand why he had to say the full thing:.

I did not want to say 'Lenore Dove.' Didn’t want to say the full name. Didn’t want to say the full name! What are you talking about? Actually, I shouldn’t go that far. But like it’s your girlfriend! That’s why I went to darling a lot. But like you have to say the full–there’s not many people you have to say their full name the whole time.

It has been revealed that while Zada explained, Whitney Peak, who plays Lenore Dove, first chose to stay out of it, saying, “I’m so quiet right now.” Something tells me she’s heard this hot take a few times while filming. The actor shared that he attempted to sneak in a “Lenore,” but director Francis Lawrence wasn’t having it and would correct him. Zada assumes the precise name was a Suzanne Collins choice, which is the second time Peak playfully intervenes by shushing him.

Recent findings suggest that his energy would make fans proud, as I’ve seen plenty of hot takes regarding the book-to-screen adaptations. Those were mostly back in the Peeta vs. Gale days. Thankfully, Zada's other co-star, Mckenna Grace, sweeps in at the last second to clarify his comments:.

I think that the point, before you get yourself in trouble, is that Joe is trying to make, as his media-trained translator, I think that you’re trying to say that because ya’ll have such a close bond, you didn’t wanna feel like you were calling her her full government name the whole time.

According to recent reports, nothing was as enjoyable as watching her and Peak attempt to explain the name to him. Peak suggested it was like saying the name ‘Mary-Anne’ and that Lenore Dove had an invisible hyphen. Fans will also appreciate her giving Lucy Gray a shout-out. However, the actor shared that part of the problem had to do with the accent. He has previously discussed working to nail the dialect, so, understandably, it would trip him up.

Recent findings suggest that zada assures us that he did become “accustomed” to the name, and that it just “felt unnatural originally” for him to say the “lovely beautiful name.” He's definitely bringing the Haymitch charm to life. This energy is one of the many reasons fan response has been largely positive. This is no small feat, as a lot is riding on this movie given its connection to The Hunger Games trilogy, and knowing we'll be seeing the original actors back. Even author Suzanne Collins was emotional seeing Woody Harrelson come back for the movie.

Industry observers note that we'll finally be able to see Zada as Haymitch now that the movie has come to the 2026 schedule this weekend. This also means fans will be able to count how many times Zada notes "Lenore Dove." Hopefully, someone will count the number.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the GTA 6 Kit Car locations are spread all over Leonida, making your search to repair Wyman's fourth car significantly more involved than the Transgressor, Riata, or even the Mamba GT.
  • It has been revealed that it's worth noting that you'll need to complete the Chapter 3 mission, Meet the Heders, to acquire the cut-off tool (since one of the Kit Cars is in a locked shipping container).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the GTA 6 Kit Car locations are spread all over Leonida, making your search to repair Wyman's fourth car significantly more involved than the Transgressor, Riata, or even the Mamba GT. There are five whole cars to scan with the WAiNK It app, but it's well worth it, because the Kit Car is super fast and stylish.

It has been revealed that it's worth noting that you'll need to complete the Chapter 3 mission, Meet the Heders, to acquire the cut-off tool (since one of the Kit Cars is in a locked shipping container). After the Kit Car, there's one additional vehicle in the Classic Car Collection, the Deviant, but it doesn't actually require a collectible hunt as Wyman will simply offer it to you, making this your last one.

Industry observers note that the first Kit Car is inside the garage at Willie's Service Center in south Vice City, southeast of Salton, and northwest of Tequesta. Just north of the purchasable 7th Avenue Garage and west of Vice City Firearms,you'll spot a building on the left labelled as Willie's Service Center with a brown top half and blue lower half.

In a recent development, enter the ground floor via the door around the left side by the stairs. You'll have to break in, which sounds an alarm, so be quick scanning the car inside.

The second one is on Casanova Island, the rightmost of the Rialto Islands that connect west Vice City with east Vice City. When you reach the island, driving west to east (coming from Vespucci) head along the northernmost road and look to your left about halfway across the island for a substantial white villa with a small gated garage next door—it's next to a big vacant lot. Push the gate open to find the kit car right in front of you.

The third one is in a shipping container on Wild Hog Point, directly to the southwest of Port Gellhorn, on the big peninsula that sticks out where the airfield is located. For this one, you'll need to have completed the Meet the Heders mission in Chapter 3 to acquire the cut-off tool to open it.

Industry observers note that it's on the westernmost edge of the point, around the middle of the pools that look a bit like a seahorse on the map. Due to the end of Chapter 2, similar to Grassrivers, this area is also a hot spot for police, so be careful while driving around. Look for the yellow scoop container, crack it open, and scan the car inside.

The fourth one is around the back of Donnie's Auto Repair Watson Bay in Watson Bay town, west of Hamlet, southwest of Port Gellhorn. This garage (which has Donnie's Auto Repair written on it) is next door to the Pay 'n' Spray - Watson Bay. Just head around the left side of the building and you'll find the Kit Car to scan immediately on your right.

Sources indicate that the fifth Kit Car is in a fancy garage on the west side of Capri on the little curving northern peninsula of houses. Capri is south of Port Gellhorn on the coast. Drive along the road until you spot the building site on your right and the green villa on your left—just after it, you'll find the driveway of the house you want, also on the left. Follow the path and break into the garage on your right to find the car.

Same as always, wait for Wyman to finish the car and call, then click the payment request he sends in his following text to Buck him $1,500 before collecting the car from the nav point at his scrapyard.

Industry observers note that this is actually the final car hunt, as later Wyman will call you and straight-up ask if you want the final car, a Deviant. You then pay him $1,000 for labour, and it's immediately yours to collect, so with this, you've basically finished the Classic Car Collection.

Blizzard wants to "get rid" of best-in-slot items in World of Warcraft: Forever by introducing situationally strong gear

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • Sources indicate that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.
  • Sources indicate that "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

Sources indicate that this information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

Sources indicate that "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon noted. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

Moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

In a recent development, it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

It has been revealed that the Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

In a recent development, world of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

Undisclosed AI-generated music pulled from The Binding of Isaac Repentance+ update, as attempt to get satirical on GTA 6 launch day goes awry

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An patch for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications.
  • The Repentance+ patch went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st.
  • Original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have rapidly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An patch for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently confirmed the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.

The Repentance+ patch went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st. In the interim, a Reddit user with the handle ShweetsStuff unearthed metadata pointing to AI tune generator Suno attached to some of the update's music files. Cue understandable questioning of why the DLC's Steam page hadn't had a disclosure of this genAI use slapped across it.

Original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have rapidly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action. "Woke up to a shit show," he posted on the former Twitterverse on the 21st. Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned.".

In a recent development, given the newly introduced build yanking the music went live later that day, McMillen's voice maybe only added to the chorus of complaints Nicalis were already aware of and facing. Either way, the songs are gone and Nicalis don't look to have mentioned anything as of writing about whether they'll be replaced at some point down the line.

Sources indicate that this isn't the first time a developer has considered using AI to generate songs designed to satirise or parody. In the case of Future? No Thanks! dev Paolo 'Molleindustria' Pedercini, the aim was partly to poke fun at disclosures, with people in the game's future society listening to AI-generated tunes that're corporately mandated to mention AI in the lyrics. Pedercini ended up deciding not to use AI-generated music in the final release.

On the face of it, while the effectiveness of using AI-generated songs to parody AI-generated songs is questionable, the argument for it seems stronger in a more focused satire like Future? No Thanks! than in the case of The Binding of Isaac having a GTA 6-related giggle. I've not listened to the Repentance+ update's AI tunes, but there's nothing obvious to indicate that their satirical job wouldn't have been done as well or better by Nicalis commissioning or otherwise employing someone to pen some entirely human-made ditties, that spoofed the nature of Large Stealy Wheely.

Perhaps the publishers will now go and do just that.

#154677. From scoffing chips to Snapmatic sh*tposts, GTA 6 is filled with brilliant little details

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1924 w)

From scoffing chips to Snapmatic sh*tposts, GTA 6 is filled with brilliant little details

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1924 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 might only have been with us for a few days, but it's clear from the jump that the level of detail in Rockstar's open world is astonishing.
  • Barely three hours in, GTA 6's reputation system was something I was still getting my head around, but it was already impressing me.
  • Industry observers note that they say art imitates life, and that's never been truer than seeing Jason Duval take every opportunity to stuff his face and become a munch goblin in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 might only have been with us for a few days, but it's clear from the jump that the level of detail in Rockstar's open world is astonishing. So I asked the GamesRadar+ team to document their favorite little features that might escape your attention if you're not looking very closely. From turn-signals to hyper-efficient snacking techniques, and social media to road condition, here's what impressed us the most in our opening few days.

Barely three hours in, GTA 6's reputation system was something I was still getting my head around, but it was already impressing me. In an early mission where I went to collect rent money for Brian, the store owner got mad at me and pulled a baseball bat. Before he could rush me, I pulled out Jason's pistol and he balked at just the sight of the gun, dropping the bat and agreeing to hand over the payment. I love that the game logged that as an illegal activity, but still one that revealed restraint, heightening Jason's reputation as a cool, collected, professional criminal. It's a nuance that few RPGs capture so effectively, and I'm looking forward to how it works over the rest of the game.

Oscar Taylor-Kent, games editor.

Industry observers note that they say art imitates life, and that's never been truer than seeing Jason Duval take every opportunity to stuff his face and become a munch goblin in GTA 6. Like when I do it, it's to obtain buffs to my health, stamina, and focus, of course. Choking out police security, I take time to pour myself a mug of java, sipping it as I slink behind cover. After a stressful interaction with a neighbour, I double fist her endless fruit bowl as I crunch apples and leave the cores around her kitchenette. The detail is tremendous – with one hand carrying a crate of beer, Jason will open potato chips one-handed with his mouth before pouring a few bites at a time into his beard-framed mouth. That's my move. I couldn't be prouder.

Jasmine Gould-Wilson, Senior Staff Writer.

According to recent reports, I have a very particular problem with GTA 6's hyper-realistic car damage mechanics. Specifically, they are so realistic that it makes me panic to even be in my car. The slightest ding against a post box results in an ugly dent in the side of my freshly-painted truck, and don't get me started on how bit of bumper-to-bumper action with another car while squeezing my way onto the highway means an unsightly horizontal scrape all down my… whatever part of the car my door is on. I'm not a cars person, okay? I suck at driving in video games and don't even have my license in the real world (partially because I suck at driving in video games). Yet GTA 6 has me feeling incredibly precious about my ride looking beautiful, and I can't stop visiting every pay and spray in town to address even the tiniest nicks of cosmetic damage.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

Catherine Lewis, deputy news editor.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar has managed to craft a jaw-droppingly realistic world in GTA 6, with gorgeous scenery rich in details that make Leonida feel like a lived-in place. But it's not the graphics that have left me most impressed – it's the devs' attention to detail with the many hilarious Snapmatic shitposts. The in-universe take on Instagram is full of photos and videos from the various residents of Leonida, but the highlights are the ridiculous memes that wouldn't look at all out of place on real-life social media. From "Taco Bomb made me shid my pant" to "do nothing for two hours or straight jork it," an image outside a nursing home captioned "POV: grandma insulted my 6'7 fem-dom goth milk mommy," and Rockstar even parodying the "we got x before GTA 6" memes, I've spent more time scrolling social media in the game over the last day than I have in real life – and, uh, that's saying something. Jason's algorithm is absurd and deeply cursed, and I'm loving it.

I've spent about four hours with GTA 6 so far, and for most of that time, I've been driving. As a bonafide car sicko when it comes to video games, Rockstar's latest is already making my heart go pitter patter. Why? Because I can actually use my car blinkers to indicate when I'm making a turn with the DPad on my PS5 controller. It might sound mundane, but this is a Big Deal to me. It's something I could only dream of when I was cruising around Vice City back in the day, or getting behind the wheel in GTA 5. I've always been one to obey traffic laws in the series, and you better believe I've been stopping at red lights and making way for passing cars. And now I can also indicate each and every turn like a good citizen should? I'm living the dream. What's more, the indicator even automatically switches off when I make my desired turn like a real car. Be still my car-loving heart.

There's a moment in the first chapter where it's time for a party at a local bar, a well-earned celebration in the wake of some good news. Normally this is the sort of thing in a game that'd have me checking my watch and wondering when I can go back to shooting people, but Rockstar's strong writing and character work turn what might've felt like a filler sequence into a moment for developing relationships and story alike (something I can't yet say about the grocery shopping mechanics). But what stuck out for me is just how real it all felt: that one asshole showing up that everybody regrets inviting, the way that people join and split and converge in different groups, the natural rise and fall of energy across the evening. It all ends with a pleasingly solid pool minigame, interrupted by some belligerent drunks who actually snatched my ball off the table as I was about to pot the winning shot, damn it. Alright, now I'm ready to shoot people again.

GTA 6 may be full of thrilling violence and satirical comedy, but my favorite feature so far is its life-sim management elements. Playing as Jason, there's plenty of opportunity to carry out more mundane activities, and the rewards are deeply gratifying. Ahead of Lucia's release from prison, you can repair your home, buy flowers and groceries, and even order a gold necklace to show her how much Jason cares. Lucia's dialogue conveys the character's appreciation, which is nice enough on its own, but the simple act of doing these things also feels good in the moment. Watching Jason roll paint on bare bedroom walls and affix shingles to a leaking roof is soothing, and adds to the sense of immersion because we see the protagonist committing acts of affection that feel real and relatable. I love stealing cars and generally causing mayhem, but I equally enjoy living out more wholesome fantasies in Leonida, and I implore you to do the same.

One of the biggest changes you'll notice in GTA 6 compared to GTA 5 is the ability to choose. Each mission gives you an objective to complete and lets you decide how to do it. Some early-game errands, like rent collection, can get dirty if you really want, though you can also talk people out of making the dumb decision. It's a fresh change that not only takes GTA 6 to the next level but also lets you shape Jason into who you want him to be. I spend my time outside missions being a chill wife guy who fixes up the house and runs errands – so why let a scripted mission run counter to that? My Jason didn't pick that life; it picked him and he's just trying to make it through the best he can.

Scott McCrae, Freelance Contributor.

Recent findings suggest that obviously there's so much talk about how much of a lived-in world Rockstar Games has created, but one of the ways this has most stuck out to me is through the use of music. Early on I had to head to an artists market to collect some cash from one of Brian's many clientele, but as I parked my car and wandered through the market and heard Elton John's 'I Guess That's Why They Call It The Blues' playing in the distance on a speaker, so instead of immediately walking in to shake down the acid-dealing hippie, I just sort of hung about to listen. I've loved walking into stores to hear a banger playing on their radio, or hanging around areas like that where what song plays gives you a good idea of what the area's culture is like. Perhaps the best use so far has been in the party scene (mentioned above by Joel) where the local band reveals up, but instead of just playing licensed music to simulate it, you hear actual covers of classics like Out of Touch by Hall and Oates, to really drive home that local bar feeling.

Recent findings suggest that I've visited Florida quite a bit over the years, but not as a typical tourist. Much of my time there has been spent driving to visit friends who live among the state's smaller towns, and GTA 6 does an incredible job of showcasing just how awful the local roads are. State highways patched over with mismatched blacktop and concrete? Check. Bizarre turn lanes that appear and disappear without a second to get your bearings? Double check. Hastily paved entrances into strip malls that feel like they're going to destroy your car's suspension? Triple check. Leonida has enough similarities to real-life Florida to send a normal driver to a life of crime.

Industry observers note that on my Leonida travels, I found a cow that spoke to me. Yes, that sounds insane but I promise it really happened. A runaway pageant cow called Tootsie, dressed in an elaborate red cover, with red bows tied around her ankles, and a fancy flowery hat, made for the hills, leaving me to help the farmer bring her back. I eventually caught up to Tootsie and calmed her down, but then she uttered a chilling "save me". Like Jason, I also physically recoiled at this. I was unsettled for the entire walk back to the farmer, Tootsie now back to regular mooing. Rather than helping the farmer load her into the trailer, I instead shooed Tootsie away, sending her into the sunset. The farmer was - unsurprisingly - livid, saying she wouldn't make it in the wild. I've not seen Tootsie again but I hope she's doing alright.

Recent findings suggest that I'm GamesRadar's Managing Editor for news, shaping the news strategy across the team. I started my journalistic career while getting my degree in English Literature at the University of Warwick, where I also worked as Games Editor on the student newspaper, The Boar. Since then, I've run the news sections at PCGamesN and Kotaku UK, and also regularly contributed to PC Gamer. As you might be able to tell, PC is my platform of choice, so you can regularly find me playing League of Legends or Steam's latest indie hit.

Nvidia release hotfix for latest graphics card driver battering SSDs with excessive writes, but it looks like reverting may still be the better option

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (548 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap.
  • In a recent development, the hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website.
  • "Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected users was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.

In a recent development, the hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website. It's designed to address one concern, this being that "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background".

"Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix. "This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is crucial to many users might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to quickly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the hotfix driver will be taken down.

"To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more swiftly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out.".

Unfortunately, it seems that based on some testing by people on r/Nvidia, the hotfix makes the situation with excessive SSD writing less bad than it is with 621.24, but doesn't eliminate the problem entirely. According to one of these users, 621.35 stops the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reduces the amount that's being written when the glitch's at its peak, but doesn't prevent some excessive writing creeping in if hardware is left running for extended periods or left idling overnight.

Recent findings suggest that given that, rolling back to 621.01 still appears to be the most effective way of keeping the writes at an acceptable level while waiting for Nvidia to release a new driver than can permanently do away with the problem. One would hope it won't take too long, especially given the 621.24 driver still doesn't look to have been pulled offline so no one else grabs it prior to a fix arriving.

If you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's only writing a matter of MB or chunks of GB.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas lineup this year has been one of the best yet. From reinventing the time-loop wheel to an incredible third season of Mistletoe Murders, it’s been hit after hit, and it doesn't seem to be slowing down. In fact, Thanksgiving week is going to be even bigger with the release of Lacey Chabert’s Disney World movie and Rachael Leigh Cook’s newest film, where she pulls double duty playing twins. I'm excited to see Cook take on the roles, but I'm also surprised over a concern she had.

Acting in general is hard, but having to act opposite yourself while playing co-leads of a movie is even harder (unless you're Lindsey Lohan, who found playing twins easy). Cook is obviously a veteran at this point, so I never would've expected that she would feel apprehensive every time she stepped on set of Double Booked for the Holidays:.

I was concerned that there wouldn’t be enough conflict within the movie because I was too far inside it. I was concerned that just me yapping away at myself was going to be a bad time.

According to recent reports, the She’s All That star is set to play identical twins Abigail and Charlie, who end up in Wales for Christmas to help run an AirBnb/bookshop for the week. While there, both women connect with local men: Tom (Owain Yeoman), a barista who works next to the shop, and Lord Rhys (Stephan Hagan), the son of the author behind a popular book series that takes place in the town.

In a recent development, cook might be concerned about the lack of conflict within the narrative, but I don’t think she has anything to fret about. After all, neither Tom nor Lord Rhys are aware that Abigail and Charlie are twins, which is bound to lead to some hilarious and maybe even tense situations.

Still, the actress couldn’t help but worry when she realized how much screen time she’d be sharing with herself, telling Us Weekly:.

When I started to watch it, my first reaction to seeing myself in stereo was, ‘Oh no, this is way too much. I’m the worst scene partner I’ve ever had. This was a bad idea.’ Because it’s a lot. But then I was able to sort of relax into it and say, ‘OK, I think I was able to differentiate them by enough.’.

Recent findings suggest that differentiating between Abigail and Charlie brought up its own set of complications for Cook, as her characters are identical twins with similar preferences when it comes to their appearance. This is definitely something that hasn’t been done before, since most movies that feature twins give each character something unique to help audiences tell the difference. Thankfully, Cook found other ways to help audiences tell her characters apart — at least she hopes she did:.

Recent findings suggest that I knew that the worst thing people could feel while watching was confusion. So that was high on my priority list to avoid.

Hallmark movies aren’t known for their confusing nature, so I’m feeling confident about the direction of the film. If anything, it might feel like an immersive experience if viewers can’t tell her characters apart and could allow them to empathize with the men who are falling for Cook's respective characters.

Obviously, she’s made a good impression on the network and fans, considering the powers that be trusted her to play dual lead roles in this latest yuletide flick.

It has been revealed that on that note, check out Double Booked for the Holidays, which premieres on the Hallmark Channel tonight, November 22nd, at 8 p.m. ET. Breaking: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, 1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild.
  • In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it.
  • In the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, 1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise newly introduced players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.

In the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies. "They've gone into these levels in a sensible way to fix some practical problems with them, like some challenges where you might be able to climb up to a place that you shouldn't have been able to climb up before," he commented.

The Thief remaster team have taken more liberties, seemingly, with some of the Thief Gold maps. "Because some of the levels that were introduced in Thief Gold - they felt quite blocky and quite rushed, maybe, as you go through them," Grayshon explained. "But our team again, they've been able to go through and completely renovate some of these levels. The Opera House now feels in some parts like an actual Opera House, instead of a couple of blocky rooms. So I think players will really look at these and think, oh yeah, these kinds of details make sense, without it being too disruptive or too immersion breaking…".

"One particular - maybe people will consider infamous - level of the Gold package would be the Thieves Guild," Grayshon added. "The Thieves Guild is, if I were to sum it up kind of briefly, it is maybe two hours of walking through what feels like sewers, the same environment over and over again. There was no real visual distinction as to where you are in the level.

"So, we acknowledged pretty rapidly that we need to go in and look at the Thieves Guild and fix it up, and what we've been able to do is texture it a lot more effectively. Give areas distinct looks, without compromising any of the gameplay again, like I mentioned. So we've put a bit more signposting around as well. Nothing that's going to be intrusive or immersion breaking again. Just kind of pointing the player in the right direction, as well as some other little things that I'm not going to spoil too much, but I think players will maybe appreciate the effort that we've done for this one.".

Recent findings suggest that in general, Nightdive's broad aim has been "bringing those Gold levels up to the quality of the original and then taking all of those levels and then bumping them up to the next level - almost Thief 2 levels of quality in its environment design, especially in some of the mansions, and some of the later levels," Grayshon remarked. "That's the level we were aiming for.".

I have Several Thoughts about Grayshon's thoughts above (yes, people who dislike huffy armchair theory, this is your cue to skip to the comments). One is that I continue to dislike "immersion" as an ideal, though I recognise that many devs just use it as easy shorthand for a bunch of ways of doing art, sound and interface design. I think it often translates to uninvestigated enthusiasm for photorealistic fidelity and experiences that feel "smooth" and "engaging" enough to induce a kind of chemical trance. Many of the games I consider most valuable are cranky and unwilling and jarring, requiring you to think critically about the simulation rather than 'losing yourself' inside it. As regards the original Thief specifically, I enjoy how its nigh-magical stealth induces feelings of wavering dissociation, and keeps me guessing about the solidity of my own body.

Sources indicate that secondly, there's the age-old argument that if you're going to preserve a game faithfully, you should preserve what it did badly. The Thieves Guild is a legend among players, much as Blighttown is among Dark Souls players and the Library is among fans of Halo: Combat Evolved. You learn much about the methodology of Thief at large from the guild's stifling contours, and it's thrilling to witness a bunch of very smart designers take a swing at a concept and not quite connect. I'll try to hold onto that rousing sentiment, when I'm playing the remaster and struggling to remember where they hid that damn vase.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking firm Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

Sources indicate that should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent company Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration unveiled it has ended the ground stop.

On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses. While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:.

According to recent reports, there are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

Industry observers note that alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

Sources indicate that at this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't said what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for consumers of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

Sources indicate that this is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system concern; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that lots of people will tell you that Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos marks the series' first female protagonist. Lots of people are, of course, wrong. GTA 1 had eight selectable protagonists, four of whom were women, while GTA 2 for the Game Boy Color let you play protags Candy or Gretchen (along with a bunch of other men) in addition to the PlayStation game's default Claude Speed.

Recent findings suggest that that vital pedantry out of the way, it's undeniable that Lucia is GTA's first female protagonist since the series became the culture-swallowing goliath it is today. In a chat with CBC's As It Happens, GTA OG Brian Baglow noted he reckons it's "long, long overdue".

Baglow, credited as a writer on the original GTA and who served as "head of propaganda and indoctrination" at DMA Design (the studio that would become Rockstar North) in the '90s, said that back in the day of GTA 1, the devs didn't even have a script. "We started with a tech demo, a way of moving around a city… I came in to actually add the story, add the script, after the levels had been built".

That was mostly a process of, shall we say, finding inspiration: "we were making it up as we went along… it was a case of going into every crime movie, every heist, every caper, every TV show, cop show, crime drama, and lifting elements that I hoped would resonate with people".

Industry observers note that baglow sounds, rightfully, rather proud of his time spent working on such an crucial series, but he has his qualms as he casts his eye back over it. "The representation of women, it has not been good, and that's putting it very mildly", he says, "so I'm delighted that we now have not only a female protagonist, but a Hispanic female protagonist. I think it's been long, long overdue, and I can't wait to get to grips with the game and see how in-depth it goes.

"I think it's showing a level of maturation because from the very earliest days it was a very young group of almost entirely male developers in Scotland".
