📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 downloadable content “Bloody Insurrection” will launch on December 17, and a Nioh 3 Complete Edition featuring the base game and both downloadable contents will launch for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store on January 28, 2027, publisher Koei Tecmo and developer Team NINJA announced.

Nioh 3 first debuted for PlayStation 5 and PC via Steam on February 6.

Here is an overview of the downloadable content and Complete Edition:.

In Bloody Insurrection, a Shogun Meets His End in Shimabara.

In a recent development, while pursuing the Spanish alchemists, Takechiyo learns that the source of Yui Shosetsu’s regrets lie in the Shimabara of the past. Guided by Shirogarasu, they transcend time once again, this time arriving in Shimabara in 1638. There, a battlefield where rebel forces, alchemists, and yokai join forces to wage a fierce and bloody struggle against the shogunate army. To uncover the source of the conspiracy, Takechiyo ventures deeper into the heart of Shimabara, encountering a host of newly introduced figures along the way, including Amakusa Shiro, leader of the rebels; Tachibana Muneshige, a legendary warlord who survived the Warring States period; and a samurai who fights back against the alchemists.

Industry observers note that shimabara in 1638. Rebels have risen up against the tyranny of a local warlord and now clash against the shogunate forces sent to suppress them. Alchemists operating in the shadows and countless yokai join the fray, turning the conflict into a brutal, blood-soaked war. Takechiyo must navigate the various landscapes of Shimabara in the battle-fraught castle town, the vast underground caverns beneath Mount Unzen, and the rebel stronghold in Hara Castle.

Fierce Battles Against Storied Characters and Newly introduced Yokai.

Takechiyo encounters Amakusa Shiro, the leader of the rebel forces, along with the legendary warrior Tachibana Muneshige, and the samurai who fights against the alchemists. Figures from Hell Rising make a comeback in this fresh story, and new yokai stand in Takechiyo’s way. There are also some familiar faces among the Guardian Spirits who lend Takechiyo their power.

New Customization Elements and Endgame Content.

New Martial Arts are being added for each weapon type, along with numerous Transformed Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, and Summoning Seals. If players have both the first and second downloadable content and manage to complete Enlightened One’s Journey (the third playthrough), they will be able to unlock the new difficulty mode and fourth playthrough, Nioh‘s Journey, where players will find equipment drops of the highest rarity, Ethereal. This will take character customization and endgame challenges to the limit.

Latest Content: The Battlefield of Carnage.

A high-volume form of endgame content, the Battlefield of Carnage, awaits players in this downloadable content. Players will need to fight their way through battlefields teeming with enemies, defeat the boss of each floor, and press onward through a relentless series of battles.

Each floor of the Battlefield of Carnage consists of a field divided into multiple war fronts. Defeat the boss controlling each war front to gain battlefield effects that provides an advantage on each floor.

Recent findings suggest that battlefield effects include steady stat boosts and other special effects. Depending on the player’s character customization, these special effects can create unexpected synergies and enable them to deliver overwhelming performances. Players are free to choose the order in which they conquer the war fronts and when to challenge the floor boss. The map provides information on the types of war front bosses and details about battlefield effects, so the player will need to devise a strategy best suited to their playstyle and character.

In addition, defeating formidable enemies on the battlefield will enable players to further strengthen equipment shrouded in traces of the Yokai Realm, which can only be obtained and generated in the Battlefield of Carnage.

Defeat the floor boss, purify the Yokai Realm, and seek out the most powerful equipment you can find. The ultimate challenge awaits, offering the hard-earned satisfaction that can only be found within Nioh.

Newly introduced Guardian Spirits, skills, Martial Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, Graces, and more.

An edition that includes the base game, as well as downloadable content #1, “Hell Rising,” and downloadable content #2, “Bloody Insurrection,” which feature upcoming stories, enemies, yokai, bosses, and equipment. The Complete Edition also includes the in-game item bonus previously offered with the Digital Deluxe Edition, the set of 14 Infernal Weapons, along with the purchase bonuses Hellfire Equipment Set and Scampuss Furball Netsuke Charm.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

It has been revealed that in an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

According to recent reports, the star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do.".

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

It has been revealed that on the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

Sources indicate that "Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that.".

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

It has been revealed that I can’t believe the release of Sunrise on the Reaping means I’ve been going to the theaters for The Hunger Games movies for nearly fifteen years! I’ll never forget when I went to see one of my favorite novels at the time become a book-to-screen adaptation back in 2012. I just rewatched the franchise and recalled one gripe I had about the movie when I first saw it that I actually understand now as an adult.

These days I think the original The Hunger Games movie is pretty great, and I’ve rewatched it so many times. I remember when I went to see it back then, I thought it was a faithful adaptation, but I was bummed that they decided to take out the fact that Peeta loses his leg in The Hunger Games. Check out this excerpt from the end of the first book:.

Industry observers note that caesar asks Peeta how his 'upcoming leg' is working out. 'New leg?' I say, and I can't help reaching out and pulling up the bottom of Peeta's pants. 'Oh, no,' I whisper,' taking in the metal-and-plastic device that has replaced his flesh.

In the movie, Peeta gets injured like in the book, but Katniss nurses him back to health, and he completely recovers by the end. Yet, in the source material, Peeta is practically bleeding out right before they become the final people in the arena. Katniss is desperate to help him, and she suggests they both have poisonous berries so she can save them both. When they reunite for the post-victory interview with Caesar Flickerman, she learns that his leg had to be amputated right after they left the arena.

According to recent reports, I think when The Hunger Games movie came out, I thought the movie was censoring an crucial aspect of the story. Peeta’s major injury really had me on the edge of my seat while I was reading the book, so it was sort of anticlimactic for the movie to completely skip it.

It has been revealed that however, it just dawned on me during my recent rewatch (with my Hulu subscription) that I haven’t thought about this change to The Hunger Games in a really long time. I guess, ultimately, it didn’t really matter that Peeta only has one leg in the scope of the whole series, and it probably would have caused some extra special effects headaches for the filmmaking team.

There’s something else. Ultimately, I’m realizing that both Peeta and Katniss have so many horrific things happen to them throughout the series that maybe it was OK for the movies to skip Peeta losing a leg. I mean, what happens to Peeta in Mockingjay alone is just heartbreaking. The guy loses his entire family, he’s captured by the Capitol and starved. And then, his brain is altered so he thinks Katniss is his enemy. That’s some really rough stuff.

Now, I think overall The Hunger Games movie series did a great job of adapting the maturity of the book series, but now I’m OK with the films taking out a few extra traumatic things like Peeta’s amputated leg.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • With Mass Effect Universe, BioWare was trying its best to account for all the endings of Mass Effect 3 in a way that preserved player choice and narrative impact but still allowed for a newly introduced story to be told.
  • That's according to Mass Effect: Annihilation writer Catherynne M.
  • Valente discusses her work with BioWare in a Reddit AMA held in support of the Save Mass Effect movement, which has seen fans call for BioWare and/or its series to be revived, and which Valente plugs in her post about the AMA.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With Mass Effect Universe, BioWare was trying its best to account for all the endings of Mass Effect 3 in a way that preserved player choice and narrative impact but still allowed for a newly introduced story to be told.

That's according to Mass Effect: Annihilation writer Catherynne M. Valente, who worked on Mass Effect Universe before BioWare was shut down and its sci-fi RPG series was put on ice. The Annihilation novel was published in November 2018 as part of the Mass Effect: Andromeda extended universe.

Valente discusses her work with BioWare in a Reddit AMA held in support of the Save Mass Effect movement, which has seen fans call for BioWare and/or its series to be revived, and which Valente plugs in her post about the AMA.

One user asked, "How did you and the rest of the team take the endings into account?" as "each one had pretty wildly different outcomes that are hard to reconcile.".

Not for the first time, Valente explains that many Mass Effect Universe details are still under NDA and cannot be shared, plus the game was very unfinished and details could shift. But she does dig into the general approach BioWare took with this narrative challenge.

"I don't think it's being naughty to say I (and not only me, but I did a lot on it) worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off," she states, "at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn't make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn't privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel.".

According to recent reports, as you may have deduced, "that's kind of a tall fucking order," as Valente puts it. BioWare had to ride multiple horses at the same time and get them all to gallop in the same direction.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

The search for "an elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn't take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible...it takes a long time, and it's not obvious how best to pull it off when you're the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing," she adds.

Sources indicate that valente reflects on the broader fandom surrounding Mass Effect. "It's become really clear that it's impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices," she says.

According to recent reports, she dismisses the argument that BioWare can simply make ME3's Destroy ending canon, noting that some players, including her, feel strongly about the Synthesis ending. So the solution BioWare had arrived at, she suggests, was decidedly not singular.

It has been revealed that "We did our best, and I think we landed in a good place," she recalls. "There wasn't one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can't say any more than that.".

She does, however, say more than that. Valente examines the role of narrative sin eater in a post-ME3 world. "I remember laughing ruefully once and thinking god, if I'd known when I finished ME3 that I'd be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess..." The worst part is that I've always gotten the impression BioWare wasn't gleefully sowing with the ME3 endings even back in the day – it's just reaping all the way down. Always those darn Reapers.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, Valente maintains that BioWare was in a good position to tackle all this. "That room was *full* of ambition and enthusiasm, and I don't think it could have been in better hands," she says. "We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it.".

Former Dragon Age lead says EA mismanagement killed BioWare by forcing it into terrible choices: "They made us do something".

He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible.

It has been revealed that GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

This state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

It has been revealed that stealing the Schafter V12 in GTA 6 is one of the car theft missions you'll have to complete to gain Raul's trust, but similar to the BF Bandito or Declasse Vamos, it's a little tricky. Make sure to grab the silenced pistol from the trunk of the car outside—not necessarily because you'll need it, but because it's a handy weapon to have.

Now, as you can see in the video above, you can get into the chop shop by climbing up the van around back and then onto the roof. I'd then suggest dropping down on the right side, where there are few enemies, knocking out the guy sitting by the gate, then opening it by hitting the left button.

Sneak back towards the centre of the chop shop and turn left to find the Declasse Vamos, a black unassuming car. Hop inside, start it up, and drive out of the gate you just opened. Easy, right? Now simply bring it to Randy's garage as directed. You also kill everyone inside if you wish, but my way above will get you that non-lethal Criminal Profile rating.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fuse Games, the developer of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has said it "didn't dream" the pod racing game's background character Biddy Blas would become as popular as he has.

Since Galactic Racer's release in October, Blas - who resembles a short, humanoid crocodile (officially a crocin) - has become a viral sensation. The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

"Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!".

Fuse Games shared a comment from Biddy Blas creator and Galactic Racer narrative designer Ren Alex-Rose about the character's success. "We always suspected Biddy Blas would be a popular member of the Galactic League, but we didn't dream of just how popular he'd become," Alex-Rose mentioned.

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole fresh level.

Recent findings suggest that "It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly.".

According to recent reports, blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who said his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer was awarded a full five stars in Eurogamer's review. "Both a surprisingly fun Roguelite campaign and a racing treat for Criterion fans, this is just wonderful stuff," wrote Christian Donlan.

As a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's crucial questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.

Recent findings suggest that in this first-person co-op platformer - created in Unreal Engine, with both online multiplayer and splitscreen support - you and a mate play Luna and Foam, two rock-hopping magic children with nothing better to do than lob hermetically sealed felines through tears in reality itself. Egad! Apparently the cats are fine with this. You'll have to work together to traverse astral watercolour landscapes, hurling and catching the kitty while trying not to tumble into the abyss.

You can also catch each other's arms and haul each other onto safe ground, which puts this in approximately the same bracket as the well-liked Peak. Other Neat Tricks include bouncing the starry-eyed moggies from soap bubbles, swinging from strands of green snot (?), and springboarding from tornadoes.

The cats remain blissfully unconscious throughout, smiling in their slumber right up to the point when you crack their crystal prisons. If you're familiar with cats, the penalty for breaking their domes may seem rather mild. I was hoping for something along the lines of Peter Puppy having a rage-out in Earthworm Jim.

Industry observers note that would it surprise you to learn that one or more of the people working on Whisk is a former developer of Sky: Children of Light, the open world swoop 'em up from thatgamecompany? I imagine you might not consider that startling – the two games both look a little like the result of somebody inhaling burnt banana skins. But you might be giddier to hear that one or more of the Whisk devs is also a veteran of Riot's Counter-Strike descendant Valorant. I'm pretty sure Valorant doesn't have any cat-throwing, but I'm prepared to be proven wrong.

It's coming to Steam early access early in 2027, and there's a demo on Steam right now with eight levels and 10 cats to "rescue". People are already bragging in the forums about their leaderboard placements – monsters!

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Google Killed Its Dark Web Report, but You Can Still Monitor Data Breaches

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let people scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers.
  • Google claims it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for consumers whose data was found on the dark web.
  • Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let consumers run scans free of cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, google’s Dark Web Report used to be the only consumer-focused platform that let people scan major data breaches, dark web marketplaces, and private forums to see if their personal information had ended up in the hands of hackers. But the tech giant discontinued the service at the start of 2026, with newly introduced scans stopping on Jan. 15 and all accounts deleted on Feb. 16.

Google claims it sunsetted Dark Web Report because, although the information it provided was generally useful, the service failed to provide “helpful next steps” for consumers whose data was found on the dark web. Google promised a upcoming service that would provide more actionable intel, but that service has yet to materialize, and there haven’t been any further announcements about it yet.

Dark Web Report may not have been perfect, but it was the only early warning system of its kind that was available for personal use and let consumers run scans free of cost. Now that it’s gone, however, there are plenty of other services that offer the same service at varying costs and levels of effectiveness. Let’s talk through the nature of the insight that Google's reports offered, how it collected that information in the first place, and what options exist in the market to replace it.

Google released the Dark Web Report in March 2023 as a premium feature available to Google One users, but later extended it for free to anyone with a Google account and moved it to the "Results about you" dashboard.

You'd set up a monitoring profile with your name, date of birth, physical address, phone number, emails, and Social Security Number if you lived in the U.S. After that, you could head to the dashboard anytime you wanted to run a free scan across dark web forums and marketplaces, publicly disclosed corporate data breaches, and other hidden online spaces to see if any of your personal information had shown up there. It was easy to use—but not a lot of people knew it existed in the first place.

It’s unclear what prompted the internal decision at Google, but in the absence of concrete next steps, it is reasonable to think the reports could create panic for the uninitiated. There’s no way to remove your information from the dark web once it’s already in circulation there. Still, having an early warning so you could reset 2FA or self-lock your SSN isn’t without merit.

But perhaps more importantly, most people with Google accounts didn’t know and hadn’t heard of the Dark Web Report’s existence. Google has likely taken it as a hint that owners want more active remediation tools than simple alerts, which is why it’s now directing users to the Password Manager, Passkeys, and “Results about you” dashboard instead—though, again, the company hasn't followed through on a direct replacement for Dark Web Report, despite teasing such a feature.

It has been revealed that many of the top dark web scanners draw from the same well of information, scanning against major data breaches and dark web spaces. Several also offer breach notifications that send you email alerts when your details show up in a periodic scan. However, none of that is worth paying for because Have I Been Pwned or Mozilla Monitor cover those features quite well for free. Even the default password managers from Google and Apple come with some ability to monitor leaked credentials.

In a recent development, there isn’t an easy way to scrub your information from the dark web once it ends up getting leaked. But you can take steps to protect sensitive information or financial data once you know there’s been a leak. If a password has been compromised, reset it immediately. Also, enable 2FA on the affected account for added security. Even better, switch to a passkey if that account supports it. If not, authenticator apps are a safer way to receive 2FA codes than standard SMS.

It has been revealed that if your Social Security number has been leaked, freeze your credit with Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can do this by contacting each agency separately. Freezing your credit will prevent unauthorized credit withdrawals and protect your credit score from abuse by attackers. If one of your credit or debit card numbers has ended up in a breach, call your bank to freeze transactions on that card immediately.

It has been revealed that finally, get in the habit of using email aliases instead of sharing your actual email address with every platform and service provider. Addy.io and Proton’s SimpleLogin are both popular services that let you generate temporary email aliases that point to your inbox.

According to recent reports, holiday time at Walt Disney World is always one of the best times to visit, but theme park fans might want to postpone their trips to the “Most Magical Place on Earth” until later in 2027. That's when all the fresh and upcoming attractions are slated to open, like the new Indiana Jones ride in Animal Kingdom. In case anyone has been wondering, Imagineers have been hard at work on the ride, and they’re finally giving fans a first look at the magic they’re crafting.

Industry observers note that the fresh Indiana Jones attraction was announced back in September 2025 at Disney’s Destination D23 event in Orlando, Florida. The news was originally met with concern from Disney World enthusiasts. It’s always exciting to see a park get a new ride, especially Animal Kingdom, which currently has the fewest amount of rides out of the four parks. However, the introduction of Indiana Jones meant the loss of the beloved Animal Kingdom attraction Dinosaur.

Time heals most wounds, though, and now that the sting of losing Dinosaur has started to wane, most fans are finally getting excited for the newly introduced attraction. To further build excitement, Walt Disney Imagineering shared the following clip on its Instagram:.

A post shared by Walt Disney Imagineering & Disney Live Entertainment (@waltdisneyimagineering).

I was definitely not thrilled about the Animal Kingdom changes at first, but I think I’m going to love this newly introduced version of Indiana Jones! I’m definitely on board with the name that was declared back at D23 earlier this year, and I absolutely love the Mayan-inspired facade. Dare I say it puts the Indiana Jones temple at Disneyland to shame (and hopefully won't have to deal with brawls over line cutting).

I Honestly Never Thought I’d Live To See The Day Disney World Fixed One Broken Attraction.

In a recent development, when the ride eventually opens sometime next year, guests will embark on an adventure alongside Indy that will take them to a temple that legend says has a water passageway that leads to an underworld protected by a mythic serpent. Imagineers are still keeping much of the actual ride experience under wraps for now. However, with two other cart-style Indiana Jones attractions at other Disney parks and reports that the Dinosaur ride is being rethemed instead of totally demolished, it’s safe to say that this version of Indiana Jones will take guests on a bumpy ride full of twists, turns, snakes (or serpents in this case), and adventure.

Indiana Jones and the Myth of the Jade Serpent will be found in the new Tropical Americas expansion at Disney’s Animal Kingdom. Specifically, the thrill ride will be part of the Bonanche Bioreseve area of the expansion, which is being modeled after the Maya region. This will mark the second Indy attraction to explore Mayan culture, but the first in the United States.

In a recent development, perhaps the most exciting thing about the newly introduced ride is that real-life Indiana Jones actor Harrison Ford was used as the model for the attraction’s animatronic. While it’s not confirmed whether or not he’ll record lines too, I’m definitely hoping he will. And if he does, then this will definitely be the best Indy ride.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

According to recent reports, there’s still a lot of work to be done on the Indiana Jones ride and the Tropical Americas land, which will include a section dedicated to Encanto. For now, fans can keep the excitement going by streaming the adventure franchise with an active Disney+ subscription.

Mark Richard Davies, game director at Naughty Dog and game designer on The Last of Us 2, is the latest game developer to appear awe-stricken in reaction to Rockstar's opus. A colleague of Davies, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet world design director Michael Barclay, recently said GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child," underscoring the unprecedented depth and scale of the game.

Sources indicate that in a upcoming tweet, Davies says we might never find every piece of the GTA 6 puzzle and jokingly predicts we'll one day discover extraterrestrial intelligence hiding in its DNA. "GTA VI is the Great Pyramids of Game Development," he says. "As in, people will be asking for centuries how it was possible and we will eventually conclude that aliens made it.".

It has been revealed that GTA VI is the Great Pyramids of Game Development. As in, people will be asking for centuries how it was possible and we will eventually conclude that aliens made it.November 22, 2026.

Industry observers note that in response to a commenter who rightfully points out Rockstar's "8 to 13" year development cycle and estimated $1 billion budget, Davis simply notes, "I'm sure the pyramids were expensive too," seemingly acknowledging that one part of Rockstar's magic is unfathomable financial resources. For instance, the thing that amazes Davies the most about GTA 6, in his words, is "Every NPC having voice lines and reactions. The sheer size of the script must be mind boggling." The level of interactivity and variety in GTA 6's NPCs is hugely immersive, but that wouldn't have been possible if Rockstar and parent tech giant Take-Two Interactive didn't have the money to pay that amount of voice and performance capture artists.

All that mentioned, in addition to lots and lots of money, there's an element to Rockstar's sterling track record for genre-defining releases that has very little to do with money and a lot to do with extremely talented individuals firing on all cylinders and a unified vision from legacy leadership. But, you know, having $1 billion dollars to spend certainly doesn't hurt.

"Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled," notes the RPG's director after entering a "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that the BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence.
  • In a recent development, kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.

Industry observers note that the BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence. On licence means his release is subject to a number of conditions. According to the UK Government website, the exact nature of these conditions varies from person to person and case to case, as they've got be "considered necessary and proportionate". However, things like needing not to commit any more crimes, not travel abroad, and live under the supervision of community offender manager are cited as part of a set of "standard licence conditions" outlined by the government site.

In a recent development, kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online. It includes bans from using both Telegram and Discord.

According to the BBC, the judge told Kurtaj Yyou are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again." City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

Kurtaj pleaded guilty on November 16th at Woolwich Crown Court to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack, as well as a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Now aged 21, he was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely, due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial.

Industry observers note that 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by the 2022 hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the firm contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

It has been revealed that earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by 'Cyberleek' posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two promptly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Cyberleek has since claimed to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 onto the net, while withholding a main executable file they threatened to release subsequently. Online sources claim the executable has now also been leaked, though this has not been independently verified.

It has been revealed that edia has declared Kendo Rage 1&2, a two-game collection featuring side-scrolling action game Kendo Rage and fighting game sequel Kendo Rage 2. It will launch for PlayStation 5, Switch, and PC via Steam on March 18, 2023.

Kendo Rage first launched for Suepr Famicom in January 1993 in Japan, followed by Super Nintendo Entertainment System in October 1993 in North America. The sequel, which never saw a localized release, launched for Super Famicom in March 1995 in Japan, followed by PlayStation in November 1995.

In Japan, Kendo Rage 1&2 will be priced at 7,800 yen for the standard physical or digital edition (8,580 yen with tax), and 14,800 yen for the physical Special Edition (16,280 yen with tax). The latter includes a copy of the game, a replica poster-style large tapestry, a soundtrack CD, and a replica flyer set.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Someone, I won't name them just so I don't get them in trouble, once remarked that EA doesn't shoot you, it puts a gun on the table and then comes in everyday and asks you if you'll shoot yourself, and they just keep coming in over and over until eventually you just are like 'Ugh, fine. Just stop bugging me about it, I'll do it.' And so the reality is that EA can legitimately say 'we didn't make BioWare do this, they chose to do this', but if you dig underneath that statement the reality is that the options on the table were all terrible. We chose the least terrible of the options." Via an interview with Pembridge.

Last month we got the devastating news that BioWare, the legendary studio that brought us Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and classics like Neverwinter Nights, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and the OG Baldur's Gate was being shut down. The decision was made by EA, just a year after it was acquired by a consortium made up of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and investment firms Silver Lake and Affinity Partners (owned by the son-in-law of US president Donald Trump, Jared Kushner).

In a recent development, the reasons? Underperforming games. Dragon Age: The Veilguard didn't hit the mark, Andromeda wasn't well received, and Anthem, the live-service shooter, shut its servers down for good earlier this year.

It's a bad string of events for sure, but former Dragon Age boss Mark Darrah doesn't believe that it's all down to BioWare's poor management. The studio was backed into a corner by EA and the pressure to perform.

Sources indicate that decisions like using the Frostbite Engine, "making Dragon Age 2", and "shipping Anthem" were all products of BioWare needing to hit financial targets set out by EA. "They basically said 'Gotta hit your financials, so what are you going to do?' Darrah says. "'Are you going to ship KOTOR a year sooner than you think is going to happen? No. Are you going to pull Mass Effect in a year? No. It was never clear what the consequence of 'no' was, and it still isn't. But it seemed really dire at the time. So you gotta do something, so what are you going to do? Did they make us make Dragon Age 2? No. But they made us do something.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, google has given its AI-powered "Ask Maps" feature a major upgrade, adding tools for trip planning, real-time route guidance, appointment finding, and saved-list search. The updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS.

Google released Ask Maps last March as an AI assistant designed to handle questions and requests more complicated than simply searching the word "bar" or "groceries." Instead of performing simple keyword searches, the idea behind Ask Maps is that you can describe several specific requirements at once, and Maps will find places that match them all. For example, you could ask for a restaurant with outdoor seating for a certain number of people, and "Ask Maps" will factor in your past searches and give you results. Of course, AI assistants have a habit of making things up, so even with today's roll-out, you'll want to double-check your sources before you drive an hour to the wrong restaurant.

Industry observers note that to me, this is the most useful newly introduced feature launching today. Whether you're planning a day trip for holiday shopping or something more ambitious, like a three-day road trip with coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Ask Maps will put together a day-by-day schedule. Each blueprint includes insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop, so you can see the whole route at a glance. Once you're happy with the plan, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.

When it's time to head out, you can ask Maps to pull up your itinerary, or look for the "itinerary" badge in your chat history. You'll see real-time details such as live traffic conditions, whether a place is currently open, and even the vibe at your next stop.

In a recent development, aims can change on the fly, too. Ask Maps to add a scenic viewpoint or a lunch spot along the way, then tap to get directions to your next stop straight from the itinerary.

Here's what else you can use Ask Maps to do, starting today.

Pulling up directions now surfaces "Know Before You Go" tips for your route. These include where to park or charge your car, along with real-time conditions like weather, potential delays, and tolls.

Ask Maps is also gaining some agentic capabilities. Allegedly, you can just ask, “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots across nearby businesses. In addition to finding appointments, Google says this agent will be able to call local businesses on your behalf—stay tuned while I wait for the upgrade and test this one out myself.

Sources indicate that if you keep lists of saved places, Ask Maps can now search them for you. Ask something like, "Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 5 in the next 30 minutes?" Ask Maps looks across your lists and checks live availability, so you can pick a place and go.

According to recent reports, these updates start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Travel itineraries and saved-list search are available everywhere Ask Maps is offered. "Know Before You Go" route tips and appointment finding are launching first in the U.S., with more regions coming soon.

Chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are right now being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

The investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

It has been revealed that the appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

Sources indicate that looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

I got as far as a fateful town gate confrontation before hitting the cap on slides for the shareware version. I mention this because upcoming, 100% "hand-drawn" first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost HyperCard game.

According to recent reports, this risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax.

It has been revealed that the plot setup here is thusly: some apocalypse cult is raising havoc on three islands off the coast of Rivelune. Five heroes – a snake minstrel, a rhino barbarian, a badger knight, a goat sorcerer and… whatever the hell critter that monk is - have been sent to investigate the whole "world is ending" sheebang and do a little levelling.

As in the very first Might and Magic, you steer the party as one, moving around a grid map. Combat is turn-based and there are "secrets, puzzles, and hidden items everywhere". Also schmürpfs. These confuse me even more than the monk character. They look like angry green omelettes. Any pointers? I googled the word and the closest match I could find was Swiss footballer Pascal Schürpf, who appears neither green nor egg-based.

In a recent development, "Every element, from sprites to textures, was hand-drawn on paper," promises the Steam page. It's out April 2027. There's no demo as yet nor even a proper trailer, but god I enjoyed looking at this, in a week otherwise full of screenshots of, like, suggestive scallion distribution in GTA 6. I should finish that HyperCard game. I still remember which river I threw the Performa into.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the late Patrick Stewart was best known for his work in Star Trek, as he became synonymous with the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard. With that, it's funny to think that the beloved star ever had reservations about joining the iconic sci franchise. Now, his friend and actor Kyle MacLachlan is opening up about that apprehension, and I can't believe I never knew Stewart rang him up shortly before he committed to The Next Generation.

Sources indicate that macLachlan caught up with SFX Magazine on CinemaBlend recently as part of a cover story publishes shortly before Stewart's death. The Twin Peaks star talked about his long-running friendship with Stewart over the decades. Noted relationship began when they worked together on the original film adaptation of Dune. A few years later, Stewart would be in the position to take on the role of Picard, and he had questions for MacLachlan before committing:.

He was about to embark on this huge experience and recognized that it could potentially be both a huge benefit and that it could come with certain... restrictions isn’t the right word, but I guess he was weighing it all up.

In a recent development, based on those comments, it seemed Patrick Stewart had some concerns about committing to a TV series, which could potentially air for a while and prevent him from taking on other roles as an actor. He probably had a lot on his mind, as MacLachlan stated, wondering if the benefit of joining Trek would outweigh the missed opportunities elsewhere.

I've written a lot in recent weeks about how Stewart rose to prominence due to being cast in The Next Generation. However, he had to put in the work to solidify his role as one of Star Trek's best characters. As Kyle MacLachlan added, though, Stewart's fears were unfounded, as he crushed it in the job and went on to be known for other roles as well:.

According to recent reports, I thought he would be spectacular in it. He’s such a strong actor, and he’s done so many different things that he would be able to fit it into his wonderful career. It wouldn’t be the only thing that he was known for, but part of a much larger tapestry.

That tapestry of work will extend to the end of the 2026 movie schedule, as the late Stewart will appear as Professor Charles Xavier in Avengers: Doomsday later this year. Stewart reportedly told co-stars backstage that it would be his final acting performance, marking his retirement. Stewart would refute those claims months later, saying that he considered acting to be something he would do his entire life.

Knowing that, and seeing that he truly was passionate about his acting career, gives me an immense amount of respect for Patrick Stewart. He worked because he loved the job, but I'd like to think he had a good deal of respect for his fans as well. Surely, between Marvel and Trek, he could've retired more than a decade ago, but he kept at it!

Recent findings suggest that the late A Christmas Carol star's commitment to his craft is a significant reason why so many fellow stars have been paying tribute to him since his passing. It's clear he was a beloved figure in Hollywood, and the world is just a little darker now that he's gone.

According to recent reports, I'm thankful for Kyle MacLachlan being bullish on Patrick Stewart joining Star Trek: The Next Generation. Had he not been, who knows if Stewart would've taken the job. Fortunately, the Fallout actor felt good about his former co-star taking on the role, and the rest is history.

Watch Patrick Stewart in TNG by picking up a Paramount+ subscription and revisiting some of his best episodes. There are quite a few to get through, and as someone who recently started rewatching the series, I know that from experience.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ho ho ho, the RPS Advent Calendar 2026 is... not ready yet. We haven’t written the words, and I keep forgetting to unblur that latest picture of Horace (drawn by the reliably talented Amanda Flagg). But while drag our lumpen feet on the business of deciding our favourite games this year, RPS readers have begun plotting, and scheming, and apparently in some cases, spreadsheeting. That’s right: the Advent Calendar Guessing Game has returned, and is open right now for keen participants.

Industry observers note that if you’re unfamiliar with this grand tradition – which is once again being run by extra-lovely reader Aerothorn on the RPS Discord – then here’s a quick rundown. You, the reader, take a guess at the 24 games we’ve chosen to hide behind Horace’s wall of advent doors this year, finalising your list before the calendar rolls out on December 1st. Once all games are revealed, those with the most accurate guesses shall bask forever in the glory of their triumph, and also bag some free access to the RPS Supporter programme. 3rd place wins a three-month subscription, 2nd place wins six months, and the 1st place Guesser Supreme wins a full year of Supp perks.

It has been revealed that be warned, though, that victory will demand a sharp mind and an impeccable memory. Or, at the very least, a willingness to go back through our reviews and What Are We Playing This Weekend posts, to remind yourself which games have taken our fancies these past twelve months. Anecdotally, I think we’ve been slightly better at actually writing about our favourites in 2026 than we were for last year’s calendar, which should hopefully make for an easier Guessing Game. If also, perhaps, a more competitive one?

It has been revealed that you can read up on the full game eligibility rules, start discussing your picks, and submit your guesses by joining the #2026-advent-calendar-guessing-game channel in the RPS Discord linked above. Note that you don’t need to correctly guess the position of an included game to earn a point for it, only its presence in the list, though you should specify which game you think will earn the coveted Day 24 door – our overall top game of the year, essentially – as this detail will serve as one of the tiebreakers in the event of a draw.

Industry observers note that thanks again to Aerothorn for setting this up, and good luck to all who participate! Here’s one hint, for free: we didn’t have Sin, Oisin, and Jeremy P voting for the Advent Calendar after having them for the RPS 100, so don’t rely too much on the latter for inspiration. Sorry, Unbeatable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the manufacturer which has long played a major role in PC gaming.

Following Huang's departure, The New York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

The report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, mentioned everyone hoped they'd drop dead.

It has been revealed that huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".

It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's said often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.

A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the New York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, said the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".

Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly said earlier this week that the manufacturer "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".
